title: Wiener attack on a small RSA private exponent
summary: Recover a sufficiently small RSA private exponent from convergents of e/n, accepting only an exact prime factorization.

signals.reason: A public exponent large relative to n is consistent with a small private exponent.

requires.reason: The continued-fraction scan requires the exact RSA modulus and public exponent.

rejects.reason: A bounded convergent scan found no exact RSA factorization.

negative_matches.reason: The modulus is already factored, so private-key reconstruction is no longer an attack-selection problem.

cheap_probes.instruction: Scan at most 4096 convergents of e/n; retain a candidate only if its discriminant is a square and the two distinct proven-prime factors multiply to n.

expected_cost.notes: At most 4096 continued-fraction convergents and exact integer checks.

tooling.reason: The bundled bounded solver uses standard-library integer arithmetic.

procedure.instruction: Copy the template into the case and supply n, e, ciphertext, and max_convergents no greater than 4096.
Treat the classical d < n^(1/4)/3 regime as sufficient, not necessary; outside it, a failed scan rejects this card but does not prove RSA security.

assumptions: RSA uses two suitably balanced primes and the secret exponent lies in the paper's sufficient small-exponent regime.

verification.instruction: Verify p*q=n, p and q are distinct primes, and e*d is congruent to 1 modulo (p-1)(q-1); decrypt and re-encrypt the supplied ciphertext.

title: RSA common modulus with coprime exponents
summary: Recover one unpadded message encrypted under one modulus with two coprime public exponents.

signals.reason: Two exponent samples under a scalar modulus match the common-modulus equation.

requires.reason: The Bezout recovery requires one modulus, two aligned ciphertexts of one message, and coprime exponents.

rejects.reason: Different messages or non-coprime exponents invalidate the direct Bezout equation.

negative_matches.reason: A list of distinct moduli is a broadcast instance, not this scalar common-modulus card.

cheap_probes.instruction: Check gcd(e1,e2)=1 and that each ciphertext is invertible whenever its Bezout coefficient is negative.

expected_cost.notes: One extended gcd, at most two modular inversions, and two public-equation checks.

tooling.reason: The bundled solver uses standard-library modular arithmetic.

procedure.instruction: Supply the scalar modulus, exactly two exponents, and their aligned ciphertexts to the copied template.
Find a,b with a*e1+b*e2=1 and compute c1^a*c2^b mod n, using verified modular inverses for negative coefficients.

assumptions: The same representative is encrypted modulo the same RSA modulus with relatively prime public exponents.

verification.instruction: Verify m^e1 mod n equals c1 and m^e2 mod n equals c2; printable decoding is not proof.

title: Hastad broadcast attack for exponent three
summary: Recover one unpadded message sent with e=3 under at least three pairwise-coprime RSA moduli.

signals.reason: Exponent three and three or more moduli form the standard sufficient broadcast shape.

requires.reason: This v1 card deliberately covers only the sufficient e=3 case with three aligned samples and pairwise-coprime moduli.

rejects.reason: Different plaintexts or shared modulus factors invalidate the direct CRT exact-root route.

negative_matches.reason: A scalar modulus with multiple exponents belongs to the common-modulus family.

cheap_probes.instruction: Check every modulus pair by gcd, CRT-combine exactly three aligned ciphertexts, and demand an exact integer cube root.

expected_cost.notes: Quadratic pairwise gcd checks for at most 64 samples, one CRT, and one exact cube root.

tooling.reason: The bundled template provides bounded CRT and exact-root arithmetic.

procedure.instruction: Copy the template and supply exponent 3, aligned moduli and ciphertexts, plus a stated maximum root bit length.
Reject the hypothesis if CRT yields no exact cube; do not round a numerical root.

rejects.reason: Identical-message samples should route to common-modulus or broadcast RSA rather than related-message gcds.

expected_cost.notes: Two degree-at-most-seven modular polynomials and a bounded gcd; composite-coefficient failures require explicit handling.

procedure.instruction: In a copied case solver, construct the two modular polynomials from the observed affine coefficients, implement a monic Euclidean gcd that surfaces non-units, require degree one, extract the root, and bound all polynomial degrees by e.

The public chunk index must be included in the normalized relation.

requires.reason: A source-anchored repeated chunk and a verified relation that includes the per-chunk public XOR counter are mandatory.

rejects.reason: The candidate slid-pair equation failed after applying the actual chunk-index normalization.

negative_matches.reason: Assuming E=F^r while ignoring the public x XOR c wrapper is explicitly rejected.

cheap_probes.instruction: From source define G_c(x)=Chunk(x XOR c), derive the candidate relation between G_c and G_(c+1), and test it on a reduced key/block model; do not test bare Chunk iteration only.

expected_cost.notes: Bound chosen texts, 24-bit table entries, normalized pair candidates, and key checks before the full search; stop on memory or query cap.

tooling.reason: The 24-bit public wrapper and chosen-text table can be modeled in bounded local Python code.

procedure.instruction: Copy the resolved challenge/src/tokencrypt.py into the case notes by immutable reference, implement the exact 16-round Feistel-plus-affine Chunk, include x XOR c before every chunk, derive normalized slid-pair filters, generate at most the recorded chosen-text/table budget, recover candidate chunk parameters, and verify complete 128-round encryption/decryption.

Record that distfiles/tokencrypt.py contains a relative reference to challenge/src/tokencrypt.py at the pinned SHA; cite both paths and analyze the resolved source, not the one-line distribution pointer in isolation.

title: Goldwasser-Micali ciphertext replication against a key wrapper
summary: Use repeated valid encryptions of one GM bit to force an all-zero or all-one AES key, then classify the challenge wrapper response; this is a challenge-protocol oracle, not a break of GM semantic security.

signals.reason: The service decrypts 128 independently submitted GM bits into an AES key.
Repeating one valid bit ciphertext deterministically repeats the decrypted key bit.

requires.reason: The authorized service must accept chosen valid GM ciphertexts and expose a stable wrapper response for at least the all-zero and all-one key controls.

rejects.reason: Without a reproducible acceptance/error class, ciphertext replication yields no wrapper oracle.

negative_matches.reason: This card targets GM-to-AES key wrapping, not CBC padding validity.

cheap_probes.instruction: Create one valid GM encryption of 0 and one of 1 from public n,x; submit 128 copies of each with AES-CBC payloads encrypted under 00..00 and ff..ff respectively, and require stable valid wrapper responses without learning p or q.

expected_cost.notes: Two 128-line control submissions plus only the separately authorized bounded search/replay queries; abort at max_oracle_queries.

tooling.reason: Public GM arithmetic and a transcript client can be implemented locally with bounded standard-library integers.

procedure.instruction: Build valid GM bit ciphertexts c=y^2 mod n and c=x*y^2 mod n with gcd(y,n)=1, replicate one selected ciphertext 128 times to force a constant AES key, construct a matching AES-CBC payload through an already available authorized tool or local primitive, submit under the case query cap, and log the full response transcript.

Describe the result as a wrapper misuse of independently decrypting attacker-selected GM bits into an application key; do not claim factorization, GM decryption, or a contradiction of the original semantic-security theorem.

assumptions: The paper defines independent randomized encryption of bits; deterministic key forcing here arises only because the challenge wrapper accepts attacker-chosen valid bit ciphertexts with repetition.

verification.instruction: Replay both constant-key control transcripts, verify every submitted value is a valid public GM encryption of the claimed bit, reproduce the AES-CBC payload locally, and confirm the exact wrapper response class.

title: Rotor wiring recovery by observed permutation conjugacy
summary: Recover rotor or plugboard permutations only after deriving an exact conjugacy relation from known mappings in the challenge log; this is a challenge-derived group model.

signals.reason: Source and log analysis identify a permutation-conjugacy recovery problem.
Known plaintext/ciphertext mappings support an exact conjugacy equation.

requires.reason: The stepping convention, known mappings, source anchor, and a faithful permutation-conjugacy toy system must be established.

rejects.reason: The proposed conjugator did not reproduce the reduced training equations.

negative_matches.reason: Independent known mappings and rotor states make exact permutation equations preferable to language-frequency guessing.

cheap_probes.instruction: Project source-derived rotor/reflector mappings to six symbols, enumerate at most 6! conjugators, and require one candidate to satisfy all training equations plus independent symbol replays.

expected_cost.notes: The bundled template enumerates at most 8! toy permutations; the 26-symbol adaptation must use cycle constraints, known mappings, and bounded branching rather than factorial enumeration.

tooling.reason: The bundled template implements exact finite-permutation composition and conjugacy checks.

procedure.instruction: Validate the conjugacy model with the bounded template, then adapt to 26 symbols by deriving cycle-structure constraints from logged known mappings, branching only over unresolved cycle correspondences, and replaying all held-out mappings.

Use the source's rotate-before-encrypt convention, rotor order, positions, plugboard involution, forward rotors, reflector, inverse rotors, and final plugboard exactly; do not substitute a generic Enigma model.

assumptions: The conjugacy reduction is derived from this exact challenge implementation and log structure; no external paper is claimed to prove the wrapper mapping.

verification.instruction: Verify every recovered permutation is bijective, the reflector/plugboard are involutions where required, all conjugacy equations hold, and the original implementation reproduces every independent log mapping and flag-format wiring.
